statements.claim: Prasena rode out of Dwaraka wearing the Syamantaka jewel and was not seen alive again; the Vrishnis and Andhakas suspected Krishna of stealing it
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.27-29: adorned with the jewel Prasena went a-hunting and was slain by a lion; hearing of his death the Vrishni and Andhaka families entertained suspicions against Krishna because they knew he had a fancy for that jewel.

statements.claim: The Syamantaka came to Dwaraka as a gift of the sun and produced gold in the palaces of the Vrishnis and Andhakas, brought timely rain, and kept disease away
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.19-25: Vivaswan took the jewel from his neck and gave it to the king; the jewel produced gold in the palace of the Vrishnis and Andhakas, the god of rains poured in due season, and there was no fear of disease.

statements.claim: Satrajit, having received the jewel, gave it in delight to his brother Prasena, who wore it everywhere
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 v.24: the king Satrajit, with great delight, conferred the peerless jewel Syamantaka on his brother Prasena.

statements.claim: Krishna desired the jewel but, though capable, never took it by force or stealth
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 v.26: Govinda grew desirous of the jewel; although capable he did not take it by force or pilfer it.

statements.claim: A lion slew Prasena in the forest for the jewel; a bear slew the lion, took the jewel, and carried it into its den
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.27-28: Prasena was slain by a wild lion for the Syamantaka; killing that lion a highly powerful bear took the jewel and entered into his den.

statements.claim: Knowing himself innocent, Krishna resolved 'I must bring the jewel' and set out with his followers, searching the mountains Rikshavan and Vindhya until stricken with fatigue
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.29-34: Krishna, thinking himself innocent, resolving 'I must bring the jewel', followed Prasena's footsteps with his followers and ransacked the mountains Rikshavan and Vindhya until stricken with fatigue.

statements.claim: Krishna found Prasena and his dead horse but no jewel, and near them the lion killed by the bear, the truth surmised from the footsteps
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.33-34: he saw Prasena and his horse killed there without the jewel, and the lion killed by the bear; it was surmised by the footsteps, and he followed them to the bear's den.

statements.claim: From inside the den a nurse was playing with the jewel with Jamvavan's son, saying 'Do not weep; the lion killed Prasena and he has been killed by Jamvavan; this Syamantaka belongs to you'
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.35-36: a nurse was giving play with the jewel to Jamvavan's son, saying 'Do not weep'; the nurse said the lion killed Prasena, he was killed by Jamvavan, and the Syamantaka belonged to the boy.

statements.claim: Krishna left the Yadavas with Baladeva at the den's mouth and entered silently with the Sharnga bow, wrestling Jamvavan for twenty-one days
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.37-40: keeping the Yadavas with Baladeva at the mouth of the den and displaying a beautiful form and voice, Krishna with the Sharnga bow entered; Govinda wrestled with Jamvavan for twenty-one days.

statements.claim: The Yadavas headed by Baladeva returned to Dwaraka and announced that Krishna had been slain
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 v.40: after Krishna entered the den all the Yadavas, headed by Baladeva, returned to Dwaraka and announced that he had been slain.

statements.claim: The clan had whispered that Krishna stole the jewel, and the rumor now went around that he was dead
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.29,40: the families suspected Krishna of the theft because of his fancy for the jewel; the Yadavas announced he had been slain.

notes: All named events, characters, places, and the nurse's dialogue match Harivamsha 1.38. Opening riding-out imagery and crowd reactions are connective atmosphere. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna had recovered the Syamantaka and conferred it on Satrajit, whose daughter Satyabhama was his wife
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.1 (jewel Krishna conferred on Satrajit was stolen) plus episode continuity (DKS_0215 pack, BP 10.56 v.43: Krishna married Satyabhama; HV 1.39 v.2 notes Akrura always wished for Satyabhama).

statements.claim: Shatadhanwa, a kinsman of the Bhoja line, slew Satrajit at dead of night, took the jewel, and made a present of it to Akrura, who exacted a promise of secrecy and swore to stand by Shatadhanwa, saying all Dwaraka was under his control
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.3-5: Shatadhanwa slew Satrajit at the dead of night, took the jewel and gave it to Akrura, who made him promise never to reveal its whereabouts and said 'If Krishna attacks you I shall follow you; the whole of Dwarka is under my control.'

statements.claim: Akrura had long desired Satyabhama and the jewel
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.2: Akrura always wished to have the beautiful Satyabhama and, on opportunity, desired to possess the jewel.

statements.claim: Satyabhama, grieving, came to her husband, told him what Shatadhanwa had done, and stood weeping by his side
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.6-7: on her father being slain, Satyabhama repaired to her husband, communicated what had been perpetrated by Shatadhanwa of the Bhoja race, and stood by his side shedding tears.

statements.claim: Krishna told Balarama that Prasena was killed by a lion and Satrajit slain by Shatadhanwa, that he was master of the jewel, and urged mounting the chariot to slay the Bhoja and recover the Syamantaka
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.9-11: Krishna told his elder brother Haladhar 'Prasena has been killed by a lion and Satrajit has been slain by Shatadhanwa; I am the master of the jewel Syamantaka; get on your car and after slaying the Bhoja Syamantaka will be ours.'

statements.claim: In the terrible encounter with Krishna, Akrura, though capable, out of wickedness did not help Shatadhanwa
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.12-13: a terrible encounter arose; Akrura, beholding both enraged, though capable, out of wickedness did not help the son of Hridika.

statements.claim: Fearful, Shatadhanwa fled on his mare Vijnatahridaya, which could cover a hundred yojanas, fighting Krishna as he fell back until the mare, spent with exhaustion and misery, died
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.14-17: stricken with fear Shatadhanwa fled; his mare Vijnatahridaya could go a hundred yojanas and with her he fought Krishna; after a hundred yojanas, on account of the exhaustion and misery of the mare, her vital breaths went up to the sky.

statements.claim: Krishna told Balarama to wait, saying he would go on foot and carry away the jewel himself
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.18: Krishna said to Rama 'Wait here; I have seen the wretched plight of the mare; going on foot I shall carry away the jewel Syamantaka.'

statements.claim: Krishna killed Shatadhanwa on the way to Mithila but the jewel was not on him, and he returned with empty hands
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.19: going on foot, Krishna killed Shatadhanwa on the way to Mithila and did not see Syamantaka.

statements.claim: Balarama demanded the jewel, Krishna said he had not got it, and Balarama, exclaiming 'Fie on you', said he forgave him as his brother, was going away, and had nothing to do with him or the Vrishnis of Dwarka, then entered Mithila
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.20-23: Balarama said 'Give me the jewel'; Krishna said 'I have not got it'; Rama, filled with anger, repeatedly exclaimed 'Fie on you', said 'I forgive you because you are my brother; I go away; I have nothing to do with you or other Vrishnis of Dwarka', and entered the city of Mithila.

statements.claim: The king of Mithila honored Balarama with presents after his heart, and Duryodhana received from Balabhadra the most excellent instruction in the use of clubs
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.23,28: Rama was honored with all becoming presents after his heart by the king of Mithila; the king Duryodhana received from Balabhadra the most excellent instructions in the use of clubs.

statements.claim: The mighty car-warriors of the Vrishni race with Krishna propitiated Balarama and brought him back to Dwaraka
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.29: propitiating Balarama, all the mighty car warriors of the Vrishni race and the high-souled Krishna brought him back to the city of Dwarka.

notes: Faithful to Harivamsha 1.39 including quoted speeches. Emotional color (Akrura 'watched from nearby', the quarrel 'began over a jewel neither brother was holding') is connective framing, not asserted fact. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: After Akrura's departure from Dwarka with the Andhakas, Indra (Pakashasana) withheld rain and drought devastated the whole country
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.30-31: after the departure of Akrura, Pakashasana did not pour rain and the whole country was devastated by drought.

statements.claim: Krishna neglected Akrura in a feat of dissension among his kinsmen, and Akrura left with the Andhakas
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.30: the foremost of men Akrura, with Andhakas, left Dwarka; Krishna, in a feat of dissension amongst his kinsmen, neglected him.

statements.claim: The Kukuras and Andhakas propitiated Akrura when the country was devastated by drought
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.32: when the whole country was devastated by drought, the Kukuras and Andhakas began to propitiate Akrura.

statements.claim: When the liberal Akrura returned to Dwarka, the thousand-eyed Indra began to pour showers on the bank of the ocean
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.33: when the liberal Akrura returned to Dwarka, the thousand-eyed Indra began to discharge showers on the bank of the ocean.

statements.claim: To please Krishna, Akrura gave him his sister Sushila in marriage
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.34: in order to please Krishna, the intelligent Akrura gave him in marriage his sister Sushila.

statements.claim: Guessing by his riches and liberality that the Syamantaka was with Akrura, Krishna told him in the midst of an assembly that the jewel was in his keeping, asked him to give it and not cheat him, and said the anger that possessed him sixty years before was now ended
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.35: guessing by his riches and liberality that Syamantaka was with Akrura, Janarddana said to him in the midst of an assembly 'The jewel is in thy possession; give it to me; do not cheat me; the anger that possessed me sixty years before is now ended.'

statements.claim: Akrura kept the stolen jewel hidden and his riches had grown on the secret
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.1-5,25: Akrura held the jewel stolen by Shatadhanwa and bound Shatadhanwa to secrecy; he devoted jewels to sacrifices and Krishna guessed the jewel by Akrura's riches and liberality.

statements.claim: Krishna suspected where the jewel lay before Akrura left; the estrangement broke open and Krishna did not call him back
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.25 (Akrura, on account of the jewel, took protective measures) and v.30 (Krishna neglected Akrura); the story's ordering is a narrative synthesis the pack does not contradict.

statements.claim: Whether the jewel passed back into Krishna's hands that day is not recorded in the sources
statements.evidence: The pack's passage is truncated at v.35 and its excerpt records only the return, the rain, and the words spoken; the story's hedge matches the available evidence.

notes: Drought description (cracked earth, failing wells, thin herds) is generic elaboration of the pack's 'whole country devastated by draught' - connective narration. Akrura 'foremost of the Vrishnis' rests on the pack's 'foremost of men Akrura' and his Vrishni identity in the lineage. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Satrajit wore the jewel at his throat and shone so brightly that people seeing him from afar had their sight dimmed and mistook him for the sun-god
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 vv.3-7: wearing the jewel on his neck he shone like the sun; people seeing him from afar had their sight dimmed by his splendor and thought the sun was coming; excerpt: 'the people of Dvaraka mistook him for the sun-god.'

statements.claim: The jewel was the Syamantaka, given to Satrajit by the sun, who was his friend
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.12-16,19: the sun was Satrajit's friend as valuable as his life; at the ocean bank the lord Vivaswan appeared and took from his neck the peerless jewel Syamantaka and gave it to him; BP 10.56 excerpt: pleased with his devotee Satrajit, Surya gave him the jewel.

statements.claim: Satrajit asked the sun for the jewel with which he lights the worlds
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.17-21: the king said 'Thou hast appeared before me as a friend but what special favour have I got' and 'O lord, it behoveth thee to confer upon me this jewel with which thou dost always light the worlds.'

statements.claim: The people followed Satrajit through the city thinking the sun was going
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.22-23: holding the jewel the king entered his own city; all the people followed him thinking that the sun was going.

statements.claim: Wearing it Satrajit shone like the sun, and the jewel yielded eight loads of gold each day and warded off all calamity
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.10 and excerpt: 'dine dine svarna-bharan astau sa srjati' (daily it produces eight loads of gold); the jewel yielded eight loads of gold daily and warded off all calamity; Satrajit shone like the sun.

statements.claim: In the older telling, gold welled up in the palaces of the Vrishnis and Andhakas and the rains came in their season
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 v.25: the jewel produced gold in the palace of the Vrishnis and Andhakas and the god of rains poured in due season.

statements.claim: Krishna grew desirous of the jewel but, though capable, did not take it by force or steal it
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 v.26: Govinda grew desirous of the peerless jewel; although capable he did not take it by force or pilfer it.

statements.claim: In time Satrajit, delighted, conferred the jewel on his brother Prasena, who wore it wherever he went
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 v.24: the king Satrajit, with great delight, conferred the peerless jewel Syamantaka on his brother Prasena.

notes: Blends BP 10.56 (eight loads of gold, sun-mistake) and Harivamsha 1.38 (ocean-bank worship, gift dialogue) as the pack does; both variants are cited in the story. Crowd color (children crying out, elders shading eyes) is connective. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna asked Satrajit for the jewel and the covetous Satrajit refused
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.11 and excerpt: though Krishna asked for the jewel, the covetous Satrajit refused (BP: he was asked by Shauri for the jewel).

statements.claim: Prasena, Satrajit's brother, went hunting wearing the jewel and was slain by a lion together with his horse; the lion was in turn slain by the bear Jambavan, who took the jewel
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 vv.12-13 and HV 1.38 vv.27-28: a lion, killing Prasena together with his horse, took the jewel; the lion was in turn slain by Jambavan (BP excerpt); HV: killing the lion, a highly powerful bear took the jewel and entered his den.

statements.claim: The jewel was made a plaything for the bear-king's child in the cave
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.14: the jewel was made a plaything (kridanaka) for the child in the cave; HV 1.38 v.35: a nurse was giving play with the jewel to Jamvavan's son.

statements.claim: The city whispered that Krishna had killed Prasena for the jewel
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.15 and excerpt: the people whispered that Krishna had indeed killed the jewel-necked one who went to the forest (Prasena).

statements.claim: Knowing himself innocent, Krishna resolved 'I must bring the jewel' and set out with his followers, following tracks through the Rikshavan and Vindhya mountains until weary
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.29-34: knowing their suspicion and thinking himself innocent, Krishna, resolving 'I must bring the jewel', followed Prasena's footsteps with his followers, ransacking the mountains Rikshavan and Vindhya until stricken with fatigue; he saw Prasena and his horse dead and the lion killed by the bear, surmised by the footsteps.

statements.claim: Krishna found Prasena and his horse dead with no jewel, the lion nearby slain by the bear, and followed the trail to the bear's den
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.33-34: he saw Prasena and his horse killed there without the jewel, and near Prasena the lion killed by the bear; following the footsteps he searched for the den of the running bear.

statements.claim: From inside the den the nurse spoke of the plaything jewel to the child, saying 'The lion killed Prasena, and the lion was killed by Jambavan; do not weep - this Syamantaka belongs to you'
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.35-36: a nurse was giving play with the jewel to Jamvavan's son, saying 'Do not weep'; the nurse said the lion killed Prasena and was killed by Jamvavan, and the Syamantaka belonged to the boy.

statements.claim: Krishna left Balarama and the Yadavas at the den's mouth and entered alone with his bow
statements.evidence: HV 1.38 vv.37-38: keeping all the Yadavas with Baladeva at the mouth of the den and displaying a beautiful form and voice, Krishna with the Sharnga bow silently entered.

notes: Faithful blend of BP 10.56.11-15 (Satrajit's refusal, rumor) and HV 1.38 (mountains, nurse's words, Baladeva at the den). 'His own cub' is an animal idiom for Jamvavan's son in the pack. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: The people of Dwaraka, not seeing Krishna emerge from the cave, thought him dead, and Devaki and Rukmini grieved
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 vv.32-33: the people did not see the exit of Shauri who had entered the cave; Devaki, Rukmini, and Anakadundubhi grieved.

statements.claim: The grieved citizens of Dwaraka cursed Satrajit, blaming his refusal
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.34: the grieved Dvaraka dwellers cursed Satrajit; the reason (his refusal sending Krishna after the jewel) is the citizens' speech, consistent with the episode.

statements.claim: Krishna returned as if risen from the dead, with the jewel restored and his bride Jambavati, the bear king's daughter
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.36: they found Krishna come back as if from death; pack index/summary: 'Krishna returns with the jewel and Jambavati'; excerpt: 'Krishna returned with the jewel and his bride.'

statements.claim: Krishna summoned Satrajit to an assembly in the king's presence, recounted the whole affair, and restored the Syamantaka to Satrajit
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.37: summoning Satrajit in the assembly in the king's presence; excerpt: Krishna recounted all in the assembly and restored the Syamantaka to Satrajit; HV 1.38 excerpt: he handed over Syamantaka to Satrajit in an assembly of the Satwatas.

statements.claim: Satrajit took the jewel with his face bowed, deeply ashamed
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.38: he, greatly ashamed, took the jewel with his face downward.

statements.claim: Satrajit resolved to give Krishna his daughter Satyabhama, a jewel among women, together with the jewel, as reparation
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 vv.39-42: reflecting on the wrong he had done, Satrajit decided 'I shall give my daughter, a jewel among women, and the jewel itself.'

statements.claim: Krishna married Satyabhama according to the rites but refused the jewel, saying 'We do not accept the jewel, O king'
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 vv.43-44: Bhagavan married Satyabhama according to the rites and said 'We do not accept the jewel, O king.'

statements.claim: Krishna told the story of Prasena, the lion, the bear, and the wrestle with Jambavan in the den, and the bear king yielded the jewel and his daughter
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.14 (jewel made a plaything for the child in the cave) and the episode's cave-wrestle sequence (DKS_0214 cluster); pack summary: 'clears his name in open assembly.'

statements.claim: Krishna had gone to clear his name, not to own the jewel
statements.evidence: BP 10.56 v.15 (rumor blamed Krishna for Prasena's death) and v.44 (he refuses the jewel); consistent with his refusing the jewel when offered.

notes: Follows BP 10.56.32-44 closely (grief, curses on Satrajit, assembly before the king, ashamed Satrajit, Satyabhama + jewel offered, marriage, jewel refused) with HV corroboration. Satrajit's inner reasoning (paragraphs on shame turning to resolution) is connective psychology matching BP vv.39-42. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Krishna was away from Dwaraka, visiting the elders of the Kuru court, when the plan was made
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.1 lists his visits to Bhishma, Kripa, Vidura, Gandhari, and Drona (Hastinapura elders); excerpt: 'While Krishna was away, Akrura and Kritavarma urged Satadhanva...'

statements.claim: Akrura and Kritavarma instigated Satadhanva to seize the jewel, claiming Satrajit had broken his word and scorned them after promising a jewel among women
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 vv.2-4: having obtained the opportunity, the two spoke to Satadhanva - 'he who, having promised us the jewel of a maiden, scorned us' - and the wicked one, his mind corrupted by those two, slew Satrajit.

statements.claim: Akrura had long wished for Satyabhama and desired the jewel once it came to Satrajit's keeping
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 v.2: Akrura always wished to have the beautiful Satyabhama and, as soon as he got an opportunity, desired to possess the valuable jewel.

statements.claim: Satadhanva, of the Bhoja line, slew the sleeping Satrajit at night and made off with the Syamantaka
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 excerpt: 'the wicked Satadhanva slew the sleeping Satrajit and made off with the Syamantaka'; HV 1.39 v.3: having slain Satrajit at the dead of night, Shatadhanwa took away the jewel.

statements.claim: The women of the house cried out like orphans
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.5: the women, wailing, cried out like orphans.

statements.claim: Satadhanva carried the jewel to Akrura, who made him swear never to reveal where it had gone and promised in return: 'If Krishna attacks you, I will follow you; the whole of Dwaraka is now under my control'
statements.evidence: HV 1.39 vv.3-5: Shatadhanwa made a present of the jewel to Akrura, who made him promise never to give out that the jewel was in his possession and said 'If Krishna attacks you I shall follow you; the whole of Dwarka is now under my control.'

notes: Clean merge of BP 10.57.1-5 (Kritavarma+Akrura instigation, broken-promise motive, sleeping victim, wailing women) with HV 1.39 (Bhoja lineage, gift to Akrura, oath). Envy framing and the two men 'believing themselves the cleverer' are connective. No unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Satyabhama found her father Satrajit slain in the night with the Syamantaka gone, and cried out 'Father, father!', feeling herself slain along with him
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.6 and excerpt: Satyabhama, seeing her father slain, was afflicted with grief and wailed 'father, father, I am slain.'

statements.claim: Her husband Krishna was far away in Hastinapura, the city of the elephant
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.7: she went to Gajasahvaya (Hastinapura, the elephant-named city) where Krishna was; BP 10.57 v.1 (Krishna visiting the Kuru elders).

statements.claim: Satyabhama placed her father's body in a great vat of oil before leaving
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.7: having placed the dead body in a vat of oil (taila-dronim), she went to Hastinapura; the preservation purpose is standard connective.

statements.claim: She told Krishna everything and stood weeping by his side
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.7 and excerpt: she went to Hastinapura to tell Krishna; HV 1.39 v.7 (episode continuity): stricken with grief and standing by his side she began shedding tears.

statements.claim: Hearing the news, Krishna wept with Balarama, following the ways of human beings
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.8: hearing it, the two lords (Krishna and Balarama), following the ways of human beings (nri-lokatam), grieved; excerpt: 'who, hearing it, wept with Balarama.'

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama mourned as a son-in-law and a brother mourn
statements.evidence: BP 10.57 v.8 (they followed human ways in grief); Krishna is Satyabhama's husband (BP 10.56 v.43) and thus Satrajit's son-in-law; elaboration of the source's nri-lokatam.

notes: Faithful to BP 10.57.6-8 (oil-vat detail, Gajasahvaya, wailing, the two lords following human ways) corroborated by HV 1.39.7 (weeping at Krishna's side). Emotional rendering (riding 'as though the news would spoil in her keeping', the closing vow) is connective. No unsupported or contradicted claims.
